drawing.vectorize.groupLevels: Draw one tone level at a time (light → dark, outline last)
drawing.hint.groupLevels: The pen finishes the lightest level before the next darker one, outline last; each level is ordered on its own to limit pen lifts. Easier to follow, and ink in different patches dries in turn, but the pen-up travel roughly triples (about 20–30 s extra for a whole drawing). Off: the whole picture is ordered together: shortest travel, but the pen hops between patches. Off by default (12/11/2026: on means more pen lifts and a longer drawing).
drawing.vectorize.bridge: Join nearby strokes inside dark areas (fewer pen lifts)
drawing.hint.bridge: When the next stroke starts within 4 line widths of where the previous one ended (Sakura 0.5: 2 mm) and the joining segment stays inside a dark area, the pen draws that segment instead of lifting and lowering. Sample A5 images: 55–80 % fewer pen lifts, 30–50 % faster, ~3 % more ink. Not used for the Outline style or multi-colour mode.
drawing.vectorize.twoOpt: Careful ordering (2-opt, slower, fewer pen lifts)
drawing.style.amFill: Even lines in light areas (no white gaps on skin)
drawing.hint.amFill: In mid-light areas (skin) the variable-wave style normally drops some lines to match the tone, leaving white gaps. On: every line is present from 10% coverage, so skin is evenly lined (slightly darker than the photo; adjust gamma / contrast if needed).
drawing.hint.soft: On: where two tone levels meet, hatch lines end at staggered points like a comb, so the tone changes gradually with no visible border line. Costs ~30% more pen lifts. Turn off to compare with the old method.
drawing.hint.outlineDetail: Low: outline only the large shapes, skip fur / wood grain / leaf texture (good for photos). High: also faint lines and soft boundaries (good for drawings, stickers, artwork).
drawing.style.outlineOverlay: Add a sketch outline layer on top
drawing.style.xdog: Use XDoG (clearer outlines on photos, dark or backlit shots)

settings.drafts.title: Drafts
settings.drafts.desc: Where G-code, preview images and parameters of created drawings are kept.
settings.drafts.help: The drafts folder is fixed (see the Data storage panel below). Pinned drafts do not count toward the limits. Over the limit, the oldest unpinned draft is deleted.
drawing.hint.blackPoint: Everything darker than this counts as pure black. Raise it (e.g. 20–40) to drop a dirty grey background; keep 0 for clean images.
drawing.hint.whitePoint: Everything brighter than this counts as pure white (not drawn). Lower it (e.g. 220–240) to drop a greyish or tinted paper background.
drawing.hint.contrast: Stretches light and dark around mid-grey. Above 1: lights lighter, darks darker, the subject stands out (flat photos, smooth skin). Below 1: softer. Usually 1–1.6.
drawing.hint.gamma: Adjusts midtone brightness. Above 1: brighter, fewer dark strokes. Below 1: darker, more strokes. Usually 0.8–1.3.
drawing.hint.maxSide: Long side of the image while processing. Empty: computed from the drawing box and pen (box ÷ pen × 1.3). Lower for faster runs on weak machines, higher to keep fine detail. Max 4000.
drawing.hint.auto_levels: Stretches brightness to use the full black–white range, so dull, grey or low-contrast photos still trace well. Turn off if the image is already well exposed.
drawing.hint.clahe: Brings out detail in locally too-dark or too-bright areas. Good for backlit photos; may amplify noise.
drawing.hint.denoise: Removes grain while keeping edges. Slow (seconds on weak machines); enable only for dim photos.
drawing.hint.kind: Zigzag: parallel hatching joined into one stroke, few pen lifts. Wave: one wavy line per row, darker means denser waves. Spiral: the whole picture is one stroke. Cross-hatching: one direction for light tones, a second perpendicular layer for dark tones (engraving look, less soaking in dark areas). Modulated wave: parallel wavy lines, taller waves where darker; continuous tone with no levels, very few pen lifts but many short segments (longer G-code). Outline: draws the borders of shapes (including where two colours meet) and ink lines, thick lines as one centre stroke; good for drawings, stickers, logos, photos with clear shapes.
drawing.hint.paletteMode: Single color: one pen, one G-code file. Multi-color: splits into 2–4 colors, one G-code file each, and you swap pens while drawing.
drawing.hint.paletteColors: Number of colors to split into (2–4), only used in Multi-color. Fewer colors are faster and need fewer pen swaps.
drawing.hint.levels: Number of visible tone steps on paper (including the white paper step): each step is a block of hatching with its own spacing, so you get that many distinct blocks (3 = coarse, 5 = more detail).
drawing.hint.angle: Hatch direction: 0° horizontal, 90° vertical, 45° diagonal. With several colors, give each a different angle.
drawing.hint.spacing: Reference distance between two hatch lines (one layer covers ~50% ink); lighter steps are sparser and darker steps tighter in proportion. Empty: automatic from the pen's real line width (0.4 pen = 0.88 mm). For Modulated wave: distance between wave lines (empty = 1.76 mm for a 0.4 pen).
drawing.hint.amplitude: Wave style only: wave height. Larger than the hatch spacing and neighbouring waves touch. Empty: automatic.
drawing.hint.outlineOverlay: Draws a sketch outline on top of the shading to keep the composition clear (good for portraits and landscapes).
drawing.hint.invert: Swaps light and dark: enable for a dark background with a light subject.
drawing.hint.simplify: Drops redundant points on strokes (mm). Larger: lighter file, faster, but less smooth. Pen 0.2 should stay ≤ 0.05; pen 0.4 can use 0.1.
drawing.hint.merge: Joins two strokes whose end and start are closer than this (mm): fewer pen lifts. Too large joins unrelated strokes.
drawing.hint.minPath: Drops strokes shorter than this (mm) to filter specks. Too large loses small details.
drawing.hint.passes: Number of 2-opt passes optimizing drawing order. 50 is enough; more barely shortens the travel.
drawing.hint.order: Orders the strokes so the pen travels less without drawing between them.
drawing.hint.twoOpt: Careful ordering, about 25% less travel but slower; switches off automatically above 15,000 strokes.
drawing.hint.xdog: Finds region boundaries with XDoG: each point is compared with its surroundings instead of one threshold for the whole image, so dark or backlit photos still get eye, nose and mouth lines. Off = the old method (Canny), good for drawings, stickers and schematics. The outline layer on top of shading always uses XDoG.

chart.help: Every run is saved automatically on the server (folder data/job_logs, last 30 kept, oldest removed when full; including runs cut short by a disconnect). Samples are taken at every machine status report (~10/s). Pen-lift counts come from the G-code, not from samples. The queue needs Bf reports ($10=3). "Download CSV" copies a file to your device; "Compare with" compares two runs on screen.
chart.error.in_use: This run is still being recorded.
chart.hint.est_ratio: Above 1 = slower than estimated (the estimate ignores acceleration). Use as a correction factor.
chart.hint.rapids: Number of G0 rapid moves in the G-code ~ number of pen lifts. Fewer = better path ordering.
chart.hint.starved_pct: Queue empty while running: commands arrive too late. High = raise baud rate or stream several lines ahead.
chart.hint.pen_down_pct: Higher = less time wasted on lifts and travel.
